name: 短嘴金絲燕

similarSpecies.distinction: Runtime House Swift taxonomy retained. More compact swift with contrasting WHITE RUMP, pale chin/throat and shallow tail fork, unlike grey-brown Himalayan rump. Current external sources lump nipalensis group into Apus affinis; no runtime taxonomic migration authorized.

Larger powerful needletail with silver saddle, short square needle-spined tail and white rear flank/undertail horseshoe, not swiftlet; comparisons not to scale. Substantive identification/range/conservation read. Sexes similar. Dark blue-gloss brown with pale SILVERY GREY SADDLE. ILL-DEFINED DUSKY GREY BROWN THROAT and DARK FOREHEAD unlike white-throated. White horseshoe rear flank/undertail and short square needle-spined tail. Distant birds very hard to separate; close head/throat views important. Monotypic breeds central Nepal/NE India/N Myanmar/S China to E Guangxi/Hainan/Taiwan, winters Thailand/Malay peninsula/Sumatra/W Java. LC stable globally; scarce HK spring passage declined locally since1990s.

rangeMap.note: 13–14cm sexes alike. Representative innominatus blackish brown upperparts with paler GREY BROWN rump not white; dark crown vs paler grey-brown nape and dark eye area; underparts paler grey brown. Blunt wing tips, slightly notched tail closed; more fluttering than House Swift. Rump colour varies, dark-rumped birds within variation, light changes apparent colours. Breeds Himalaya to central China/Myanmar/N Thailand/SW China; winters Bangladesh/Malay peninsula. Regular nonbreeding S China/N Vietnam, vagrants Taiwan/Korea/Japan excluded partial map. LC stable; scarce increasing HK visitors all months. Partial native-country overview only, not complete or exact occurrence/season polygons; green not whole-country occupancy.
